# Digitakt II: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-11, research snapshot `2945a822544d`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Brief version: rules, recovery, bugs, incidents and open questions. The full pack [digitakt-2.md](digitakt-2.md) adds all facts.

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitakt II

- **C1** (C) One mod = one OS version. Addresses and stock bytes are version-specific (hash-pinned). A mod for Digitakt mk1 1.53 is refused on 1.54; Digitakt II 1.17 addresses do not carry to 1.18+. Porting = find every address again. Keep a separate build per OS version. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {digitakt2-perform}
- **C10** (C) Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers. Call stock routines in the emulator and compare with what they must return (complex-ping's check found that its SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply); measure one timing per project on the unit and carry the ratio (2x on the DT2 for DDR-reading code, 7-12x in one digimod case, a hard stop that overshot 3x as far). An emulator that agrees with itself proves nothing about silicon. The display is part of this: digikit's emulator showed intro frames upright that the panel showed upside down. Check one asymmetric picture on the unit before trusting the emulator's orientation. Incidents: [I36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x), [I37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i37-a-sharc-emulator-shifted-every-fractional-multiply), [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {digimod} {dn2-skill-md} The same holds for event fields: Modwerk read a knob's own push-button byte as FUNC, and an emulator reference screen lacked markers the unit draws. Incidents: [I55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i55-a-knobs-own-push-button-byte-was-read-as-func), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit).
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [hw] Test your DIN interface before you need it. On a DT2, a generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) delivered nothing, while a controller's DIN out worked. Cheap cable adapters are known to drop or mangle long SysEx; a stock-OS dry run with your exact cable is the only proof. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} ([I44](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing)) (`recovery#73f47f95`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L20))
- [doc] Digitakt II OS 1.16 is no longer on Elektron's download page (author suggests asking Elektron support). Keep stock files you may need. `[doc]` {digitakt-ii-research} (`recovery#5a9efa40`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:25](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L25))
- [doc] Two upgrade paths: from within the OS (Transfer, DROP page, confirm with YES on the device; devices whose OS does not fully support Transfer are sent to the LEGACY OS UPGRADE page) and from the Startup Menu (device's MIDI port, not USB; hold FUNC while powering on; TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; Transfer in LEGACY OS UPGRADE mode). `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#67684a45`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L28))
- [doc] "Some upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap" right after the first restart; do not turn the power off then. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#065677fb`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L29))
- [doc] Downgrading is not supported and is at the user's own risk; user content may be lost. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#258d6d79`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L30))
- [doc] Digitakt II, first reboot after upgrading to OS 1.15: a file-system integrity check (up to a minute). On errors: back up all projects and samples with Transfer, SETTINGS > SYSTEM > FORMAT +DRIVE (tick SAMPLES), re-import. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} (`recovery#00f8aff4`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L31))
- [doc] Heat +FX: in-OS path is SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with the file sent through MIDI In or USB MIDI In; the startup path takes MIDI In only. `[doc]` {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#2a7bab5e`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L32))
- [doc] Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research `RECOVERY.md`): keep an official stock `.syx`, a physical MIDI interface and cable ready; MIDI OUT of the interface to the Digitakt II's MIDI IN (USB MIDI cannot be used); hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; in Elektron Transfer open the SYSEX TRANSFER page and choose "OS upgrade via device startup menu"; select the stock file and keep power on until the unit reboots. No durations are given and the author states recovery is not guaranteed if the startup menu or bootloader cannot run, power is lost during a critical write, or storage/hardware is damaged; the page reports no hardware test of the procedure. `[doc]` {dt2-recovery} (`recovery#2c2f6817`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L35))
- [doc] Digitakt II: hold FUNC while powering on, press the key the startup menu shows; project slot 001 is overwritten with the factory project and the loaded project is cleared; sound/preset bank A is overwritten; other slots/banks untouched; samples on the +Drive are kept. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-support} (`recovery#40019018`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L62))

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I70** A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller. Cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause. Fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes. Rules: A39.
- **I14** DAG registers stored through their own DAG hung the DSP. Cause: `DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar; the PRM forbids it and stock never does it. Fix: move DAG registers through an R register. Rules: A33.
- **I15** A frequency shifter froze the unit at boot. Cause: a selas defect left a nested hardware-loop end compressed; code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. Fix: `.NOCOMPRESS` around nested loops; cache write-back before running copied code. Ran on send and master 2026-10-30. Rules: A45,A28,A41.
- **I16** A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed the unit. Cause: the ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards. Fix: keep the decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes. Rules: A46.
- **I17** Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit. Cause: per-sample accesses to stock buffers in external DDR (`0x8045b3c0`). Fix: render into L2 and copy once per block. Rules: A52.
- **I18** The flash cave reportedly froze a unit at the logo. Cause: not settled ([CONFLICTS O18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md)). Fix: check the bytes the other cave users leave; prove the cave on a hard run. Rules: A43.
- **I23** Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at PREPARING. Cause: not stated; the author says not to assume the route is reliable everywhere. Fix: power cycle and the startup menu. Rules: A20,A36.
- **I27** An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip. Cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR). Fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly. Rules: A41,G9.
- **I36** The emulator undercounted DSP time by 2x to 12x. Cause: the emulators model no memory stalls. Fix: budget with silicon costs; leave a margin; measure once per project on the unit. Rules: A35,C4,C10.
- **I41** A label defined twice resolved to the wrong file. Cause: a label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object. Fix: unique label prefixes per file. Rules: D4.
- **I53** Boot-screen frames were upright in the emulator and flipped on the panel. Cause: the emulator decodes the intro bitmap as if the intro flush flipped like the main-UI blit. On the panel, intro rows are stored top-down mirrored. Why the intro path differs (flush routine or panel scan direction) is not established. Fix: digikit's `.dkbs` frames, safe screen and pixel helper use the panel's layout. The emulator decoder is not fixed yet. Rules: C10,D13.
- **I61** Odd jump targets froze a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator kept running. Cause: byte-aligned code sections put routines at odd addresses; a jsr/jmp to an odd address stops the ColdFire with an address error (vector 3), while the emulator keeps running. Fix: the linker refuses an odd-target absolute jsr/jmp into mod RAM; each code section starts with a 2-byte alignment. Rules: A42.
- **I67** Code built into .bss crashed a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator ran the zeros. Cause: two new routines were placed in `.bss` instead of the code section, so the unit jumped into zero-filled memory. The emulator executed the zeros as no-ops and booted. Fix: the routines are code again in 2.6.1. The README says not to flash a 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6 build; Digi2MacroOSC and Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM still name core 2.4. Rules: A42,C10.
- **I44** Recovery used on a Digitakt II after a crashing build; a cheap cable delivered nothing. Cause: the cable. Fix: rehearse recovery with your exact cable and the stock file. Rules: A11,A36.
- **I54** Safe mode by REC at power-on, tested on a Digitakt II. Cause: test. In the emulator, digikit's earlier queue scan missed the key (`safe:0`); reading the stock key state fixed it. On the unit, a key held at power-on does produce a report. Fix: — Rules: A29.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O20** DT2/DN2 stock intro frame rate: A) 30 Hz: digikit's PIT3 model (PCSR `0x093f`, PMR 8593), so the first scene table's 175 frames last 5.8 s (finding 117) B) 15 Hz: digikit's earlier emulator notes derive it from divisor 1024 (66.67 ms per frame; finding 07)
- **O18** DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` at boot: A) unusable: "digikit's flash_cave (0x403117c4) froze the device at the logo: that trailing region is not loaded or is cleared on the hardware, whatever the emulator does" (a comment in dt2-capicola's build script, vendored in dt2-machine-lab) B) usable: Deja Vu's releases put their payload there and were validated on a unit for boot and operation; 70b185's builds put a stub there and run on a unit; digikit's canary survived boot in its emulator
- **O7** Free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17: A) static: free up to `0x200fa000` (digikit finding 100) B) the owner's unit: clicks and delay leaks past `0x200f5a74`
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H2** (stock) Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once. Test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.
- **H3** (stock) A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid). Test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?
- **H5** (stock) Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01). Test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?
- **H19** (stock) The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20). Test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).
- **H24** (stock) The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too. Test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.
- **H6** (probe) The DT2's SHARC DDR above the sample pool window (`0x9d22b9c8` up to `0xa0000000`, about 46 MB) is never written by stock, as the DN2's tail `0x80531000-0xa0000000` is not. Test: dnfw's method: fill the range with a pattern at boot, then scan it during heavy playback, pattern and kit changes, FX extremes, sample loads and a save. Expect a reserved top part for Capicola builds only.
- **H7** (probe) The DT2's ColdFire runs the same FreeRTOS layout as the DN2: higher priority numbers run first, prio 0 never runs, prio 1 is the idle loop; the main task's stack is barely used. Test: With the USB probe: find the ready table and the running-task pointer, sample them 60 times.
- **H9** (probe) The DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` is safe on a stock image; the freeze report (O18) came from something else in that build. Test: A stock image plus a canary in the cave, read back after a cold start after a long power-off (A40).
- **H14** (build) The SHARC's IIR0/FIR0 accelerators compute on the DT2 exactly as measured on the DN2 (output from stored word 5, FIR sums in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round). Test: Port the accelprobe image to the DT2 and compare the 76 result words.
- **H20** (build) DT2 OS 1.17 saves only the kits the user changed, so a module's own kit data that changes by itself is lost unless a stock parameter of that kit changes too. Test: Modwerk publishes a unit procedure: change only module data, save, power-cycle, reload.
- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T7** (needs unit + custom engine, effort L) Find the cause of the sticky "bitcrush until reboot"
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)
- **T14** (needs unit + emulator, effort M) Fix or document digikit's EMAC fractional-mode emulation against a unit measurement
- **T15** (needs unit, effort M) Probe free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17 between `0x200f5a74` and `0x200fa000` on a unit
- **T18** (needs files, effort M) Document the project file formats (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`) beyond song slots

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).
